ai.title: Refactor CLI menu with diagnostics and responsive layout
ai.summary: Overhauls `npm-app/src/menu.ts` to replace static help text with a structured interface. Implements a `DIAGNOSTICS CHECK` section that detects Git repos, `.gitignore`, `knowledge.md`, and `codebuff.json`, providing specific remediation hints. Adds responsive command rendering based on `process.stdout.columns`, using a simplified list for terminals under 100 chars. Removes unused imports (`picocolors` default, `CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS`) and updates color application logic to use direct key indexing.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant in a project folder, it now shows a quick setup check at the top of the menu instead of a long list of help text. This check looks for a code project (a Git repository), a file that tells the tool which files to ignore (.gitignore), a project guide (knowledge.md), and the tool's settings file (codebuff.json), and it tells you which ones are missing and how to add them. If your computer screen or terminal window is narrow, the menu switches to a simpler, one-item-per-line layout so nothing gets cut off; wider screens keep the full formatted logo and aligned columns. The change is live today for anyone who starts the assistant.

ai.title: Removed invoice.created handler from Stripe webhook
ai.summary: Removed `handleInvoiceCreated` function and its `invoice.created` case from `web/src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts`. All invoices are now charged at zero dollars, making the credit note creation logic for draft invoices obsolete. The change affects only the Stripe webhook processing in the web app.

eli5.text: The system no longer creates special credit adjustments when a draft invoice is first generated by your payment processor. If the webhook previously logged that it had created a credit note for usage-based billing and you rely on automatic zero-dollar invoicing, those credit notes will stop appearing for draft invoices. This is a behind-the-scenes reliability improvement and does not affect invoices that are already paid.

ai.title: CLI enforces singleton Client via createInstance
ai.summary: npm-app/src/client.ts converts `Client` constructor to private, adding `createInstance` and `getInstance` static methods to enforce a singleton pattern. npm-app/src/cli.ts removes the `private client: Client` property, replacing direct instantiation with `Client.createInstance` and subsequent calls with `Client.getInstance`. This centralizes client state management and prevents duplicate WebSocket connections within the CLI process.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the assistant software now keeps tighter control over the single connection that talks to the server it chats with, instead of letting multiple copies of that connection get opened at once. This is internal housekeeping that affects anyone running the program on their own computer, and if you watched closely you'd see the program sets up that connection once and reuses it rather than starting a fresh one each time it needs to talk.

ai.title: Enable self-review prompt and cast assistant messages
ai.summary: Re-enabled self-review system instruction in backend/src/main-prompt.ts by removing the false condition. Added castAssistantMessage to map filtered history, ensuring correct message types for the review step. Scope limited to backend main prompt logic. Self-review now triggers whenever assistant messages exist in history.

eli5.text: The assistant now reviews its own previous answers before continuing a conversation, so you are less likely to carry forward a mistake. It does this by adding a short instruction that tells the assistant to check past messages for errors and gently correct them as if it were fixing its own work. This only happens when the assistant has already replied in the same conversation; simple one-off questions are unaffected. The feature is live today in the backend that powers the assistant.

ai.title: Saxy StringDecoder hardcodes utf8 encoding
ai.summary: Saxy constructor now instantiates StringDecoder with hardcoded 'utf8' instead of reading defaultEncoding from _writableState. Removes conditional check and fallback logic that guarded against undefined state or defaultEncoding. Scope limited to common/src/util/saxy.ts. Eliminates reliance on internal stream state properties for encoding resolution.

eli5.text: You may have noticed that some text processing in the app was occasionally behaving unpredictably when dealing with character encodings. The developers fixed this by simplifying how the text handling works internally, making it consistently use the standard 'utf-8' encoding instead of trying to guess what it should use. This behind-the-scenes adjustment makes text handling more reliable, though you're unlikely to notice any visual difference day-to-day. The change is live now.

ai.title: Set defaultEncoding utf8 in Saxy constructor
ai.summary: Explicitly sets `defaultEncoding: 'utf8'` in the Saxy Transform constructor options. This ensures consistent string handling for incoming data chunks, preventing potential undefined default encoding issues. The change applies to the shared core utility `common/src/util/saxy.ts`.

eli5.text: The software now explicitly tells one of its internal tools how to read incoming data by setting a default text format, instead of leaving it to guess. This prevents rare moments where text could get misread because the tool wasn't told the expected format. Most people won't notice any difference unless they rely on consistent handling of text data.

ai.title: Add index on message finishedat
ai.summary: Added btree index `message_finished_at_idx` on `message.finished_at` in migration `0015_stormy_zuras.sql`. Optimizes query performance for filtering or sorting messages by completion time. Updates `common/src/db/schema.ts` to reflect the new index definition.

eli5.text: The app now keeps a quick-reference list of when each message finished, so screens that show messages sorted or filtered by completion time load faster instead of sifting through every message each time. You won't see a new button or setting, but if you open a list heavy with completed messages, it simply appears without the usual pause. This is already live today for anyone viewing message lists, and developers will find the matching reference recorded alongside the rest of the database layout so the optimization stays in sync as the app evolves.

ai.title: Add composite index on finishedat and userid to message table
ai.summary: Migration 0016_clear_hairball.sql drops single-column index message_finished_at_idx and creates composite index message_finished_at_user_id_idx on (finished_at, user_id). This optimizes queries filtering by both user and completion time. Update common/src/db/schema.ts and run migration to apply.

eli5.text: Messages you've already finished now load faster, because the app looks them up using a combination of the account that owns them and the time they completed rather than just the completion time alone. Behind the scenes, the app's filing system was switched from a single column to a two-column lookup (completion time plus account), so searches that filter by 'my finished messages from today' no longer have to scan every message in the system. The improvement is live for anyone whose account stores finished messages, and you would notice it mainly as pages that list completed messages loading smoothly under normal traffic. The app now uses a composite index named message_finished_at_user_id_idx that covers both finished_at and user_id, replacing the old single-column index.
